title: traffic-muted warm-standby certification runner and kv-prefill smoke-harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated certification runner that exercises warm standby readiness without impacting production traffic (traffic-muted mode). The runner will: 1) inject controlled synthetic traffic that follows realistic request distributions (latency/seq_len/model variant mix), 2) prefill KV cache and verify cache hit-rate thresholds, 3) validate model-variant fallback logic under capacity constraints, 4) surface readiness scores and failure categories to Console and the failover runbook. This ticket focuses on the harness, instrumentation, and a single canary workflow to certify a regional standby prior to cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic-muted runner can execute a 10k-request certification pass against a standby region without routing any production user traffic.
KV cache prefill step achieves >= 85% prefix hit-rate for the canonical prompt set used by the cert harness within the first 90s of the run.

Fallback model verification: when primary variant is artificially limited, requests must automatically route to configured fallback variants and the runner verifies output sanity for a curated prompt set.
Readiness score computed and posted to Console endpoint /certification/last-run with breakdowns (cache_hit, avg_p95_latency_ms, fallback_rate, error_rate).
Failure taxonomy and automated short-circuit decision documented and linked to the regional failover playbook.
implementation_notes: Create a new cert-runner service (stateless job) that can be invoked from CI or scheduled via orchestration pipeline.
Runner will use traffic-muting VPC mirror + synthetic request generator to avoid impact to live routing tables.
KV-prefill implementation: replay prefix-heavy synthetic sequences + verify server-side observed cache metrics via Prometheus scraper.
Fallback verification: introduce rate-limited kernel-level circuit that denies new primary variant allocations to simulate capacity exhaustion.
Telemetry: emit structured events to telemetry ingestion with tags: run_id, region, model_variant, step, metric.
Expose run results as JSON artifact (s3) and push a summarized card to Console via existing internal API.
